Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

example noun

also for example, for instance, instance, object lesson, give an example, give me an example, set a good example

classical

Cic. Phil. 13.2: exemplī causā paucōs nōmināvī
Traupman 146: exemplum praebet
Traupman 222
Traupman 311

exemplum, exemplī n.

noun, second declension

an example, an instance; a model to follow

Exemplī causā or grātiā, for example; exemplum dare or praebēre, set an example (Tac., Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ut — as, for instance (before the example)

    conjunction · also used · classical · Traupman 221: genus masculīnum, ut “hic magister”

  • 1puta: short final a (Traupman 171, 272 putā). Lewis & Short, s.v. putō: pŭtă, imperative, used for “for example”.

    puta1 — say, for instance

    imperative of putō, used as an adverb · also used · classical · Hor. S. 2.5.32: Quīnte, puta, aut Pūblī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 171, 272: ut putā

    (poetic and post-Augustan (L&S))

  • documentum, documentī n. — a lesson, an example, a warning

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 156

    Lewis & Short: what teaches, an example or a warning.

Examples

  • longum iter est per praecepta, breve et efficāx per exempla

    the road through rules is long; through examples it is short and effectiveSen. Ep. 6.5

  • ducēs exemplō potius quam imperiō, sī prōmptī, sī cōnspicuī, sī ante aciem agant, admīrātiōne praesunt

    leaders lead by example rather than by command: if they are ready, if they are seen, if they fight in front, they lead because they are admiredTac. Germ. 7.1

  • exemplī causā paucōs nōmināvī

    I have named a few, by way of exampleCic. Phil. 13.2

  • Dā exemplum.

    Give an example.Traupman 222

  • bonum exemplum praebēre

    to set a good exampleTraupman 311

See also lesson, detail, model.
